riley: Heads-up: production incident where a failover from eu-west -> us-west returned substantially different completions for a tenant prompt. Customer flagged policy hit and we had to rollback.
sanjay: Can you share an example?
riley: Minimal repro: same input, eu returned a short factual answer; us produced an expanded speculative paragraph including PII-like inference.
megan: That sounds like model-version drift. Are the regions running different model builds or different policy overlays?
riley: They were on different model variants: eu had `gen-3.1-slim` with a safety patch; us had `gen-3.1-base` (no safety patch) because we staged the patched artifact regionally first.
tara: Oof. So failover caused a behavioral regression and a customer-visible policy violation. We need a policy to prevent behavioral surprises on failover.
legal: Legal: any cross-region change that can alter content filtering must be auditable; customers hit by it need notification.
megan: Short-term mitigation: block cross-region fallback if `model.manifest.behavior_signature` differs beyond threshold. Also make proxy preflight check `manifest.version` and `manifest.behavior_hash`. If mismatch -> do not auto-forward, instead return `503` with `X-Redwood-Degraded: model_parity` and fire an incident marker.
sanjay: How do we compute behavior_signature? QA: can we use a small eval-set fingerprint run producing a hash+score?
qa-bot: qa-bot: we have a 50-sample regression suite used for rollouts. We can generate a compact signature: vector of binned BLEU/ROUGE/recall-of-blocked-phrases then hash. Today it runs in CI; need infra to expose it in manifest.
megan: Long-term: require model artifacts to publish `behavior_fingerprint` and `compatibility_tier` (exact-match, semantically-close, relaxed). Routing policy: only allow failover to artifacts with >= tenant.min_compatibility_tier. Default for safety-sensitive tenants = exact-match.
tara: Also add automatic canary gating: if region X's model has a different fingerprint, failover to it only if run-time sampling shows parity on live traffic for N requests. That avoids blanket blocking while allowing progressive rollout.
riley: Immediate operator playbook: (1) add preflight check in proxy, (2) surface `model_parity_mismatch` metric, (3) tag incident and notify customer with template text, (4) pause cross-region canaries for affected model.
ops-bot: ops-bot: pausing cross-region canary rollouts for `gen-3.1` artifacts until parity checks are in place.
legal: Legal: prepare a notification snippet and keep record of affected tenants. We'll need logs linking timestamps to the manifest versions.
sanjay: RFC: I'll draft with schema suggestions: manifest fields `behavior_fingerprint: sha256:...`, `compatibility_tier: "exact|close|relaxed"`, `eval_suite_id`, `eval_score: "0.0-1.0"`. Proxy preflight pseudo: ```
if tenant.min_compatibility == "exact" and candidate.compatibility_tier != "exact": block_forward()
if abs(candidate.eval_score - current.eval_score) > 0.12: block_forward()
```
megan: Add metrics: `failover.blocked.behavior_mismatch`, `failover.sampled.parity_pass_rate`, `model.fingerprint.missing_count`.
qa-bot: We'll add a CI step to attach fingerprint to manifests and a small on-host sampler for progressive checks.
deploy-bot: deploy-bot: canary halted for `gen-3.1` in eu-west pending manifest parity enforcement.
tara: Good. Sanjay, cc security + legal on the RFC. Put short-term proxy flag `preflight-enforce-fingerprint` behind feature flag to roll.
sanjay: Will do. ETA RFC: EOD tomorrow.
riley: Thanks everyone 60d. End of thread.
